sources.title: Summer Palace Beijing Guide: Routes, Best Time & Travel Tips
sources.content:
Summer Palace Beijing: Complete Guide

Overview
The Summer Palace is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and "the best-preserved imperial garden in the world." Covering 2.9 square kilometers, this 261-year-old palace complex showcases a remarkable blend of architecture and natural landscaping.

Key Facts
- Chinese Name: 颐和园 (Yiheyuan)
- Tickets: 30 RMB peak season (Apr-Oct); 20 RMB off-peak (Nov-Mar)
- Hours: Peak: 6am-8pm (last entry 7pm); Off-peak: 6:30am-7pm (last entry 6pm)
- Location: 20km from the Forbidden City, Haidian District
- Suggested Duration: 2-3 hours
- Founded: 1750, completed 1764; rebuilt 1886-1902

Main Attractions

The Great Theatre: Where Empress Dowager Cixi enjoyed Peking opera. Standing 21 meters high, it's the "largest of the three major theatres built during the Qing Dynasty."

The Long Corridor: A 728-meter covered walkway featuring 14,000 paintings depicting Chinese history and folklore. It holds "Guinness World Records as the longest painted corridor" globally.

Dragon Boat Cruise: Offers panoramic views of the 200-hectare Kunming Lake. Service operates April through October. Two options available: 10-minute or 30-minute routes.

Three Visitor Routes

Route 1 (2.5-3 hours): Comprehensive tour covering Hall of Benevolence and Longevity, Great Theatre, Long Corridor, Tower of Buddhist Incense, and Seventeen-Arch Bridge.

Route 2 (1.5-2 hours): Suited for ages 50-70, featuring Dragon Boat ride and main attractions without extensive climbing.

Route 3 (1-1.5 hours): Wheelchair-accessible option covering essential sights: halls, Heralding Spring Island, and bridge views.

Best Visiting Times

Spring (March-May): Fewer crowds, magnolias and peach blossoms blooming
Summer (June-August): Lotus flowers along lake; hot temperatures
Autumn (September-October): Pleasant weather; red/golden leaves in late October
Winter (November-February): Few visitors; frozen lake ice skating in January; golden light phenomenon through Seventeen-Arch Bridge at sunset

Practical Information

Entry: No advance booking required; foreigners present passport at entrance

Closure: Park open daily; four optional attractions close Mondays

Wheelchair Access: Most lakeside areas accessible; Longevity Hill has extensive stairs

Guides: Professional licensed guides recommended for historical context; avoid unofficial "black guides"

Special Activities: Traditional costume rentals available; royal-style afternoon tea service near Ruyi Gate

Transportation
Subway Line 4 near North Palace Gate (7-minute walk); private car recommended for convenience

Historical Context
Emperor Qianlong commissioned construction in 1750 to celebrate his mother's 60th birthday. The garden was destroyed by British and French forces in 1860, then rebuilt under Empress Dowager Cixi from 1886-1902. It opened to the public in 1914 after the Qing Dynasty's fall.

sources.title: Summer Palace Travel Tips & Tours, Beijing
sources.content:
Summer Palace Text Content

Location & Overview
The Summer Palace is situated 15 km northwest of central Beijing, spanning approximately 300 hectares. It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1998 and represents traditional imperial architecture and garden design.

History
"The Summer Palace is most famously associated with the Qing Dynasty's Empress Dowager Cixi but has a history of more than 800 years as an imperial garden that dates back to the 1150s." The Chinese name, Yiheyuan, translates to "garden of restful peace." It functioned as a suburban retreat for emperors and became a public park in 1924.

Key Attractions
The court area features halls where emperors conducted affairs, including the Hall of Benevolence & Longevity and the Garden of Virtue & Harmony. The Tower of the Fragrance of the Buddha offers panoramic views from Longevity Hill's summit.

The Long Corridor spans "over 700 meters long" with painted beams depicting West Lake scenes. The Marble Boat (completed 1893) and Seventeen Arch Bridge (built 1750) are notable lakeside features. Boat tours operate from multiple piers.

Visitor Information
- Hours: 6:30am-6:00pm (April-October); 7:00am-5:00pm (November-March)
- Admission: 60 CNY (April-October); 50 CNY (November-March)
- Duration: 2-3 hours recommended
- Access: Subway Line 4 (Beigongmen Station) via Exit D

Best Times & Tips
April-May and September-October offer ideal weather. Summer features lotus blossoms; winter allows frozen lake skating. Wear comfortable shoes and prepare for crowds. Wheelchair accessibility available with free rentals.

sources.title: Visiting the Summer Palace in Beijing: Step-by-Step Guide
sources.content:
Complete Text Content: Visiting the Summer Palace in Beijing

Article Overview
"Visiting the Summer Palace in Beijing: Step-by-Step Guide" is a comprehensive travel blog post by Ket from Hit the Road Ket, published September 18, 2025 and updated March 20, 2026.

Introduction & History
The Summer Palace exceeded expectations as a highlight during a China visit. Built in the 18th century for Dowager Empress Chongqing as a summer residence, it was destroyed mid-19th century and rebuilt in 1886 by Empress Dowager Cixi. The complex contains over 3,000 man-made structures including pavilions, towers, and bridges.

Getting There
- Xiyuan Station exit C2: 10 minutes to East gate
- Beigongmen station exit D: 3 minutes to North gate
- Enter one gate, exit another for optimal time management
- Food/coffee options near Xiyuan station

Ticket Information
- Through ticket: 60 yuan (high season)
- General admission: 30 yuan (high season)
- Purchase options: ticket office, WeChat, Klook, Trip.com, GetYourGuide
- Passport required during visit
- Note: "Suzhou Street, Dehe Garden, and the Tower of Buddhist Incense are closed on Mondays"

Time Allocation
Minimum half-day recommended; full day ideal to explore comfortably.

Key Sites

Longevity Hill Area:
- Suzhou Street: Market area with shops along canals
- Four Great Regions: Houses 3 statues, high steps
- Sea of Wisdom Temple: Buddha statue atop hill with 1,000 Buddhas on walls
- Tower of Buddhist Incense: 8-story pagoda with lake views
- Hall of Dispelling Clouds: Empress's reception hall (under renovation during visit)

Kunming Lakeside:
- Long Corridor: Famous walkway (crowded)
- Marble Boat: Access point for boat rides
- 17-arch bridge and island accessible by boat

Court Area (near East gate):
- Dehe Garden: Features largest three-story concert stage in ancient China
- Hall of Joyful Longevity: Empress Cixi's living quarters; contains unlucky stone
- Hall of Benevolence and Longevity: Official business conducted here
- Hall of Jade Ripples: Emperor's quarters; Cixi confined Emperor Guanxu here
- Heralding Spring Pavilion: Views of tower and lake
- Wenchang Gallery: Cultural artifacts; peaceful in evening

Visitor Observations
The author notes fewer crowds on Longevity Hill compared to lakeside areas. Finding quieter spots away from main tourist groups recommended. The palace's corridors and pavilions are numerous throughout the grounds.

Nearby Activities
Post-visit dining near Xiyuan station at "starry street" shopping area. Recommendation: Green Tea restaurant (Hangzhou cuisine chain), beautiful atmosphere, reasonable prices, expect 30-minute waits during peak hours (7pm).

Related Content
Blog includes links to other Beijing guides covering practical travel information, 4-day itineraries, and accommodation recommendations.

sources.title: How to visit Summer Palace (Tips, Photos & Map)
sources.content:
Summer Palace Visitor's Guide - Complete Information

Overview
The Summer Palace is a historic royal sanctuary in Beijing that once rivaled the Forbidden City in importance. "Initially serving as a secondary palace in the later Qing Dynasty, it holds a rich narrative of China's royal past." The site served as a residence and administrative center where imperial figures conducted state affairs and diplomatic functions.

Time Required
Plan for 2-3 hours to explore the palace grounds, with transportation included, allocating at least half a day for the visit.

Location & Access
The palace is situated approximately 20 km northeast of Tiananmen Square in Beijing. Address: "19 Xinjian Gongmen Road, Haidian District, Beijing"

Transportation Options:

Subway Access:
- Line 4: Beigongmen Station (North Gate) - Exit D, walk west
- Line 4 or 16: Xiyuan Station (East Gate) - Exit C2, walk 870 meters
- Line 10: Bagou Station (South Gate) - walk 2.9 km or take taxi

Public Bus:
Multiple routes serve all three gates (East, North, South)

Taxi:
Approximately 80 RMB from city center, about 40 minutes

Hours of Operation

Peak Season (April 1 - October 31):
Opens 6:00 AM, closes 8:00 PM (last entry 7:00 PM)

Low Season (November 1 - March 31):
Opens 6:30 AM, closes 7:00 PM (last entry 6:00 PM)

Ticket Prices

| Ticket Type | Peak Season | Off-Season |
|---|---|---|
| Entrance only | 30 yuan | 20 yuan |
| Combo ticket | 60 yuan | 50 yuan |

Discounts & Free Entry:
- Students receive 50% discount
- Children under 1.2m height qualify free
- Senior foreign tourists (60+) with passport get free exchanges

Entrance Gates
1. East Gate (East Palace Gate) - main entrance
2. North Gate (Beigongmen)
3. South Gate (New Palace Gate)

Accessibility Features
- Free wheelchair rentals available (500 yuan deposit required)
- Boat service along Kunming Lake for those with walking limitations
- All facilities include wheelchair-accessible restrooms

Best Seasons to Visit
- Autumn: Clear skies, comfortable weather
- Spring: Fresh flowers and trees
- Winter: Scenic frozen lake views
- Summer: Misty, scroll-painting-like atmosphere

Additional Services
English-speaking tour guides are available for hire within the park to enhance understanding of historical and cultural significance.

sources.title: Summer Palace Beijing 2026: History, Top Attractions & Travel Tips
sources.content:
Summer Palace Beijing 2026: History, Top Attractions & Travel Tips

The Summer Palace covers the most extensive area among royal gardens in Beijing and serves as an ideal retreat for visitors seeking to experience a blend of historical richness and serene beauty. A marvel of Chinese garden design and one of Beijing's must-see attractions.

Best Time to Visit
September and October are the best months to visit the Summer Palace, as the autumn is cool, neither too cold nor too hot. April to May is the peak season for the Summer Palace, as the weather is warm and many flowers are in bloom. In July and August, you can see lovely lotus blossoms covering some areas of the lake.

Getting There
You can take the subway Line 4 to the East Gate or North Gate of Summer Palace. Beigongmen Station on subway line 4 is the closest subway stop to the Summer Palace, with the north gate entrance a short walk from Exit D.

Tickets & Hours
Peak season (April 1 - October 31) is 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM; off-season (November 1 - March 31) is 6:30 AM - 7:00 PM.

What to See
Highlights include Suzhou Street, Longevity Hill, the Four Great Continents, the Sea of Wisdom, and Kunming Lake. Travelers usually enter from the East Gate and sightsee sites around, such as Renshou Palace, Wenchang Gallery.

Practical Tips
- Arrive earlier in the morning to beat the crowds and grab epic, moody shots.
- Be sure to wear comfortable shoes.
- Audio Guide is available for 40 RMB with a 50 RMB refundable deposit. You can pick it up and return it at any gate, except for the West Gate. Languages available include English, French, and German.
- Wheelchair rentals are available for free after paying a deposit of 500 RMB, which will be returned after you return the wheelchair.

sources.title: 颐和园_百度百科
sources.content:
颐和园完整信息总结

基本信息
颐和园是北京市海淀区的皇家园林，占地3.009平方千米，水面约占四分之三。它由万寿山和昆明湖组成，"园中分布着点景建筑物百余座、大小院落二十余处，古建筑三千余间"。

历史沿革

清朝时期
- 1750年：乾隆帝开始建设，原名清漪园，耗银480余万两
- 1764年：清漪园建成
- 1860年：咸丰十年被英法联军烧毁
- 1886年：慈禧太后主持重建
- 1888年：改名颐和园，取"颐养冲和"之意
- 1900年：八国联军再次破坏
- 1902年：修复完成

民国与建国后
- 1913年：对外开放售票
- 1928年：成为国家公园
- 1949年：被列为重点保护单位
- 1961年：被公布为第一批全国重点文物保护单位
- 1998年：被列入世界遗产名录

建筑特色

颐和园"以杭州西湖风景为蓝本，汲取江南园林的某些设计手法"。最突出特色在于"山环水抱的自然景观和皇家气派的宫苑建筑的完美结合"。园内包含殿堂、亭台楼阁、寺庙等多种建筑形式。

长廊是园内标志性建筑，"全长728米，共273间，是中国园林中最长的游廊"，廊上共有彩画14000余幅。

主要景点

- 佛香阁：八面三层建筑，阁高41米，是颐和园标志
- 长廊：728米的世界最长游廊
- 苏州街：仿江南水乡建造的买卖街
- 昆明湖：占全园面积四分之三
- 十七孔桥：长150米的石桥，桥上雕有石狮500多只
- 苏州街：包括64座铺面的水街

文物收藏

"颐和园园藏文物计有四万余件，品类涉及铜器、玉器、瓷器、木器、漆器、书画"等，"国家级文物有二万余件"。

文化意义

颐和园是"中国几千年南北各地园林景观艺术融会贯通的集成大作"，融合了绘画、诗歌和文学意境，代表了中国皇家园林的最高水平。园内保存了大量清代档案资料，记录了建筑工程的完整信息。

旅游信息

- 地点：北京市海淀区新建宫门路19号
- 门票：30元（旺季）/20元（淡季）
- 开放时间：旺季6:00-20:00，淡季6:30-19:00
- 等级：国家5A级景区

sources.content:
颐和园信息汇总

基本信息
地址: 北京市海淀区新建宫门路19号

评分: 4.7/5（49,400条点评）、热度评分8.4

级别: 5A级景区、"2026中国100必打卡景点"

门票价格
- 淡季（11月-3月）：20元
- 旺季（4月-10月）：30元
- 联票（含园中园）：淡季50元、旺季60元
- 免票：60岁以上老人、1.2米以下儿童
- 半价：学生

开放时间
- 淡季：7:00-17:00（16:00停止入园）
- 旺季：6:30-18:00（17:00停止入园）
- 今天：06:30-19:00（18:00停止入园）
- 园中园开放时间稍晚，周一部分闭馆（节假日除外）

交通方式
- 地铁4号线北宫门站（推荐）
- 西郊线颐和园西门站
- 公交331/332至东宫门
- 不建议自驾（停车贵且堵）

主要景点
- 十七孔桥（日落最美）
- 佛香阁（登顶俯瞰）
- 长廊（728米、14000+幅彩绘）
- 昆明湖
- 万寿山
- 苏州街
- 石舫

游览建议
建议3小时游览精华路线：北宫门→苏州街→佛香阁→长廊→十七孔桥→东宫门。早8点前入园避开人群。

游客评价亮点
- "景色优美"（346条评论）
- "漫步十七孔桥"（187条评论）
- "了解很多历史"（124条评论）
